title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E is a constructible Q_l-sheaf (more generally a complex in D^b_c) on a scheme X that is proper over F_p, with structure map f: X -> Spec F_p. The L-function is L_E(t) = prod_i det(1 - tF | H^i_c(X̄, E))^{(-1)^{i+1}}, where F is the geometric Frobenius. DE = RHom(E, K_X) is the Verdier/Grothendieck dual, with K_X = f^! Q_l the dualizing complex.

Step 1 (global duality). Because f is proper, Rf_! = Rf_* and Rf_*(DE) ≅ D(Rf_*E). Taking cohomology gives H^i_c(X, DE) ≅ H^{-i}(X, E)^∨, and this is Frobenius-equivariant: F acts on the dual by the contragredient, i.e. the transpose inverse.

Step 2 (linear algebra). For a space V of dimension n with automorphism F, det(1 - tF | V^∨) = det(1 - tF^{-1} | V) = (-t)^n det(F)^{-1} det(1 - t^{-1}F | V).

Step 3. Insert this degree by degree, using (-1)^{-j+1} = (-1)^{j+1}. This gives formula (1):
L_{DE}(t) = (-t)^{-χ(E)} δ(E) L_E(t^{-1}), where
- χ(E) = rank Rf_*E = Σ(-1)^i b_i, with b_i = dim H^i(X̄, Ē), and
- δ(E) = Π_i det(F | H^i)^{(-1)^i}.
Grothendieck labels χ the 'invariant géométrique' and δ the 'invariant arithmétique'.

Step 4 (margin). Assume X smooth and E lisse and pure (or a Tate twist of something pure), granting the Weil conjectures / 'conjectures standard'. Then |det F on H^i| = p^{(i+w) b_i / 2}. So δ(E) = ε(E) · p^{Σ(-1)^i (i+w) b_i / 2}, with ε(E) of absolute value 1.

Top boxed formula: the special case where E is self-dual up to a Tate twist (Ě ≅ E(q)). Combined with Poincaré duality, this gives the classical shape L_E(1/(p^? t)) = (const) · t^{?} · L_E(t), where the constant is an 'élément du groupe de E' and arises from the identification Ě ≅ E(q).

Purpose: a sketch of the cohomological proof of the functional equation for L-functions of l-adic sheaves over finite fields, i.e. the SGA 5 programme. The central idea is to isolate the constant of the functional equation as an arithmetic invariant of E.
errors: The δ(E) line writes H^i(X̄, F̄) where E is meant; this is a notational slip.
The crossed-out line 'χ(DE) ≅ D(χ(E))' was rightly abandoned. χ(DE) = χ(E) holds as an integer, and the statement only makes sense as a class in K_0. It was replaced by Rf_*(DE) = D(Rf_*E).
Formula (1) holds only if Frobenius on the dual acts contragrediently, which is the correct convention. With that convention the sign and exponent -χ(E) check out.

The exponent (i+?)/2 in the margin is only correct under purity hypotheses (X smooth proper, E lisse pure of weight w). At the time these were conjectural (Weil/standard conjectures), as the margin itself says.

ideas.what: Functional equation of L-functions of constructible l-adic sheaves on proper varieties over F_p, deduced from global Verdier/Grothendieck duality Rf_*D = DRf_*
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Verdier duality and the functional equation L_{DE}(t) = (-t)^{-χ} δ L_E(1/t)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 5, 1965–66; SGA 4½ 'Fonctions L modulo l^n et modulo p' by Deligne)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (exposés on duality and L-functions; Exp. XV); SGA 4½ (Deligne's rewrite)

ideas.what: Constant of the functional equation as the alternating product of Frobenius determinants on cohomology, called an 'invariant arithmétique' and separated from the 'invariant géométrique' χ
ideas.modern_name: Global epsilon factor ε(X,E) = det(-F | RΓ_c)^{-1} (determinant of cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 5); local decomposition conjectured by Deligne (1972–74), proved by Laumon (1987, product formula)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 Exp. XV (functional equation with constant); not the local product formula

ideas.what: Under the Weil/standard conjectures, the absolute value of the constant is a power of p determined by Betti numbers and weights, leaving a unit (sign) ε(E)
ideas.modern_name: Purity / Deligne's Weil II weight bounds applied to epsilon factors

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean working sketch of the SGA 5 functional equation, and it is correct. The labelled split into a geometric invariant (χ) and an arithmetic invariant (δ, the global ε-factor), with an absolute value conditional on the standard conjectures, is a nice glimpse of the motivation. But all of this is in SGA 5, and the later ε-factor theory of Deligne and Laumon covers it. No new result is present.
transcription_corrections: 'H^i_c(X, DE) ≃ D(H^{-i}(X,E))' is followed in the right margin by 'vu le th. de dualité globale', confirmed.
The margin notes read 'invariant géométrique' (for χ) and 'invariant arithmétique' (for δ).

The bottom marginal note reads roughly 'avec les conjectures standard ... permet de mieux ... si X var. [lisse] et F ct. tordu [pur de poids] p', i.e. a purity hypothesis. The '?' in the exponent (i+?)/2 is most likely the weight.
In the δ(E) formula, 'F_{H^i(X̄,F̄)}' denotes the Frobenius on H^i, and 'det' precedes it.
